Experiment_description: A minimal SemanticLens baseline pipeline is implemented as a seed exploration. ImageNet validation images are used as probes to extract ResNet-50 layer4 channel activations (post global-average-pooling). For a subset of channels, top-k activating probe images are identified, embedded via a local CLIP vision tower, and per-channel mean pairwise cosine similarity is computed as a concept-consistency score. A matched-size random baseline is constructed for comparison.
Significance: This establishes an end-to-end working pipeline linking CNN internal components to a shared vision-language embedding space, and provides a first quantitative signal that top-activating images for a channel are more semantically coherent than random image groups. The positive delta over the random baseline validates the core premise that individual CNN channels encode coherent concepts extractable via CLIP embeddings, forming a foundation for subsequent semantic labeling and interpretability analyses.
Description: The pipeline: (1) loads ImageNet-val parquet as probe images; (2) loads ResNet-50 and hooks layer4 to extract channel activations after GAP; (3) for a subset of channels, finds top-k activating probe images; (4) embeds those images with a local CLIP vision tower using manual preprocessing (avoiding AutoImageProcessor) with defensive tensor extraction; (5) computes mean pairwise cosine similarity per channel as concept-consistency; (6) builds a matched-size random baseline; (7) saves v_c pooled vectors and histograms. Robustness safeguards include a preflight smoke test running 2 images through both models before the main loop, and a fallback path if CLIP's get_image_features returns a non-tensor.

List_of_included_plots.description: Histogram of sorted concept scores / activation distribution across ResNet-50 components on the ImageNet probe dataset. Right-skewed with most values in the lower range and a heavy tail extending to higher values.
List_of_included_plots.analysis: The sparsity pattern (most channels weakly activated, a few strongly firing) confirms that top-k reference-input selection is meaningful and non-degenerate, supporting the mechanism of identifying concept-specific probe images per channel.

List_of_included_plots.description: Histogram of activation magnitudes for ResNet-50 components on ImageNet probes, heavy right-skewed with long tail.
List_of_included_plots.analysis: Confirms proper activation extraction and typical ReLU sparsity, serving as a sanity check that the hook-based feature extraction is functioning correctly.

Key_numerical_results.description: Mean concept consistency score (mean pairwise cosine similarity of CLIP embeddings of top-k activating images per channel) on ImageNet val / ResNet-50 layer4.
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Establishes a baseline coherence level of channel-top-k image sets in CLIP embedding space.

Key_numerical_results.description: Median concept consistency score across channels.
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Median close to mean indicates a fairly symmetric per-channel consistency distribution, not driven by a few outlier channels.

Key_numerical_results.description: Random baseline mean cosine similarity for matched-size random image groups.
Key_numerical_results.analysis: High baseline reflects natural cosine similarity structure in CLIP embedding space; must be subtracted to interpret concept-specific coherence.

Key_numerical_results.description: Delta between concept consistency mean and random baseline mean.
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Positive delta validates the core hypothesis that top-activating images per channel are more semantically coherent than random groupings, though the modest magnitude suggests room for improvement (e.g., better channel selection or embedding calibration).
Provides a scalar tracking objective for subsequent iterations to improve upon.
